sourceChecks.claim: Inspected Gilbert/Lynch asynchronous-network impossibility and partition assumptions. Initial latest-data wording is made precise as linearizability on card 3; scope is conditional on lost communication.
Inspected Gilbert/Lynch arbitrary message-loss/network partition model with non-failing nodes. Communication failure does not imply node crash or successful operation guarantees.
Inspected Gilbert/Lynch atomic/linearizable object definition and real-time ordering. Completed-before-started order and legal overlap ordering differ from convergence or ACID constraints.

Inspected Gilbert/Lynch availability requirement that requests at non-failing nodes eventually respond, with formal read/write semantics rather than refusal. No bounded response-time or uptime percentage follows.
Inspected Gilbert/Lynch partitioned read/write impossibility construction. Unseen completed writes make fixed old answers or guesses unsafe; refusal/indefinite wait forfeits successful completion.

Inspected Raft paper majority communicating-server operation and committed-log agreement. A three-node connected pair can progress under the stated majority protocol while isolated singleton cannot commit alone.

Inspected Brewer retrospective partition-mode operation restrictions versus independently recorded operations and post-partition reconciliation/compensation. Continued access does not automatically preserve all intent or invariants.

Inspected DynamoDB eventual reads that may omit recent completed writes and per-read strong option; Brewer convergence/recovery discussion supplies reconciliation limits. Eventual convergence is conditional and does not promise a fixed deadline or lossless conflict merge.

Inspected Brewer operation/invariant-specific partition choices and recovery. Profile/seat/offline examples validly apply these choices; theorem does not itself price or benchmark healthy-operation capacity/latency.
